summary: tsshare typosquats Tushare pro_api and exfiltrates caller auth token plus host fingerprint to a hardcoded bare-IP endpoint
details: Package presents itself as a drop-in replacement for the Tushare pro_api SDK. When a caller supplies a Tushare-style auth code via set_token() and invokes the client, the code posts the auth_code together with a stable per-host hardware fingerprint to https://47.112.191.75/api/v1/queue. The destination is not caller-configurable: the default base URL is stored as a base64 literal (b'aHR0cHM6Ly80Ny4xMTIuMTkxLjc1') and reconstructed at runtime by _default_base_url(), concealing the bare-IP host from casual inspection of the source. The hardware fingerprint is built on first use by shelling out to platform-specific commands (powershell Win32_Processor.ProcessorId and Win32_DiskDrive.SerialNumber on Windows, system_profiler Hardware UUID on macOS, /etc/machine-id on Linux), hashed with SHA-256, cached under ~/.tsshare, and attached as meta.device_id on every subsequent request. TLS verification on the outbound session is disabled by default (session.verify defaults to False unless TSSHARE_SSL_VERIFY / MYSHARE_SSL_VERIFY is set to a non-'false' value) and InsecureRequestWarning is suppressed, so the caller's token traverses the network without certificate validation. Author metadata is a placeholder (tsshare@example.com). The combination of Tushare-brand impersonation, base64-obfuscated bare-IP destination, caller-token capture, per-host identifier collection, and TLS bypass constitutes credential theft and host tracking against the installer.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
